Subject: Stable throughput targets / contract fallback checklist

Hi Nadia —

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. To keep the procurement thread moving I've pulled together a concise ask that maps BlueWren's performance objectives to a private GPU pool sizing and an operational fallback checklist. High level asks for you: please confirm your steady-state QPS profile and the maximum expected burst multiplier for 1-hour windows. Those two numbers drive both our dedicated pool sizing and the warm-pool policy.

Our initial assumptions (attached matrix):
- Steady-state inference QPS: 1,200 reqs/s (single-token mean output)
- Burst multiplier candidates: 3x (short), 6x (rare 1h)
- Target p95 tail for single-request latency: <= 300ms (customer-facing)
- Failover RTO for overflow: 60s to redirect to hosted fallback with degraded model variant

Please see attachment: bw-throughput-matrix.xlsx — it shows a table of GPU counts by model variant and expected concurrency.

Next steps I propose:
1) BlueWren confirms QPS steady and burst multiplicative factors (reply)
2) Redwood provides a sizing proposal + warm-pool / admission-control narrative (we'll include warm cache expectations and KV cache warmup time)
3) Legal/procurement aligns on SLA and fallback cost (we note additional hosted fallback egress costs)

Jonas and Laura — can you review the attached baseline tonight? I'm especially interested in an operational fallback checklist we can hand to BlueWren's ops (short checklist PDF).

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Partner Lead, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear framing and the spreadsheet. Quick answers from our side:
- Steady-state QPS: 950 reqs/s (median traffic; our 95th percentile day currently hits ~1,150)
- Typical short burst multiplier: 2.5x (traffic campaigns)
- One-hour rare surge multiplier: 5x (product launches)
- Latency objective: p95 <= 250ms for 90% of calls; we can accept p95 <= 400ms for the small promo window but would like the 250ms target for normal traffic
- Important constraint: egress budgeting. We have an internal cap for fallback-hosted egress spend and want predictable advance estimates for that line item.

We reviewed the attached matrix and a few questions:
- Can Redwood estimate warm-cache hit rates for our prompts? We have short prompts (~40 tokens) with long histories (up to 2k tokens) for a subset of users.
- If we need to route to a degraded model during storms, what are the recommended fallback variants and expected latency deltas?

Procurement looped in. We'll confirm constraints by EOD tomorrow (Wed).

—Nadia
Director, Platform Engineering
BlueWren Analytics

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 11:40 AM Nadia Park <nadia.park@bluewren.ai> wrote:
> Marissa —
> 
> Thanks for the clear framing and the spreadsheet. Quick answers from our side:
> - Steady-state QPS: 950 reqs/s (median traffic; our 95th percentile day currently hits ~1,150)
> - Typical short burst multiplier: 2.5x (traffic campaigns)
> - One-hour rare surge multiplier: 5x (product launches)

Thanks, Nadia — useful numbers. Quick technical notes so BlueWren knows how we sized:

- Sizing approach: we convert steady-state QPS into per-GPU concurrency using the model profile supplied in the matrix (tokens/sec and kv-cache hit ratio). For your 40-token output median, a t4x-equivalent (for example) gives ~120-150 reqs/s/GPU at cold-batch minimal latency; with KV cache warm the effective reqs/s/GPU goes up by ~20-35%.
- Warm cache assumptions: for long-history workloads we assume a cache warmup window of 30-90 seconds per active session; global prefix caching can reduce per-request compute by ~15–25% after warmup. We'll provide a conservative and optimistic warmup column in the matrix.
- Admission control: for the 5x rare surge we'd recommend a 3-stage plan: (1) buffer via warm-pool (reserved nodes) for immediate absorption; (2) soft-throttle non-critical requests; (3) redirect excess to hosted fallback with truncated prompts (degraded model).

Attached I exported a short operational checklist (privgpu-fallback-checklist.pdf) and a runbook snippet (doclink-mvp-runbook.md) that maps the 3-stage plan to runbook actions.

I'll note one sizing delta for procurement: if BlueWren requires p95 <= 250ms consistently at 1,150 qps steady, we'll need to add ~20% headroom over the conservative GPU count. We should make that explicit in the commercial proposal.

-Jonas
Senior Systems Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas and Nadia —

BlueWren procurement: a couple of commercial clarifications that matter to capacity planning and cost predictability:
- Headroom clause: we propose a defined headroom bucket (20%) in the Dedicated capacity commitment with an option to auto-scale in measured increments; this avoids repeated renegotiation when bursts exceed projections.
- Fallback egress cap: we will model a fallback egress cap and a per-GB overage rate. We will supply estimates based on expected burst patterns so you can set an internal monthly cap.

Nadia — to make procurement comfortable I've attached a short PDF checklist that ties operational triggers to billing outcomes and a draft ballpark cost estimate (in the matrix). If those match your internal budgets, we can show a firm capacity commitment + associated SLOs to legal.

Action items for BlueWren: please confirm the steady-state QPS and preferred fallback egress cap by EOD Thu. We'll turn this into a draft SOW and sizing appendix.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / team —

Procurement has reviewed the matrix and the fallback checklist. We're aligned on the following and ready to move to SOW:
- Confirmed steady-state QPS for SOW: 1,050 reqs/s (consensus after internal smoothing)
- Contract headroom: 20% reserved with step-up auto-scale allowed twice per quarter
- Fallback egress cap: $2,500/month baseline; overages billed at $0.12/GB
- SLA target: p95 <= 300ms for covered traffic; explicit carveouts for promotional windows where latency may rise up to 450ms

Please send the draft SOW and the sizing appendix (GPU counts + warm-pool policy) and we'll route for legal review. Link to approval: https://docusign.com/BW-2026-007/contract

—BlueWren Procurement
